shouldFix.title: Two retained pin records still do not enumerate an advisory roster under v10's every-pin rule
detail: pinChainRule is unqualified: 'Every pin record enumerates the full blocker, shouldFix, and advisory roster of the file it pins.'
codexv6 and codexv7 each enumerate blockers and shouldFix but have no advisories member. Every other retained pin record in v10 carries all three members.

An omitted member cannot distinguish a measured empty roster from an unmeasured or lost roster. The dispatch did not permit opening those older review files, so this review does not infer their contents; the defect is the absence of the enumeration the subject itself requires.
The named CLAUDE-V9-B1 repair is accurate for claude2v8 and codexv8, but honestyRepairsFromV9 overstates closure of the class-level rule while these two records remain structurally nonconforming.
shouldFix.impact: The current v8/v9 repair evidence is auditable, but the supposedly exhaustive pin ledger still contains two records whose advisory standing cannot be recovered from the structured entry alone.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Re-measure each pinned Codex review and add its exact advisories array; use [] only if the frozen file actually has zero advisories. Alternatively scope pinChainRule prospectively, though an exhaustive ledger is preferable.

shouldFix.title: The primary-cardinality failure branches do not determine what is refused or which native writes survive
detail: multiplePrimaries is only the bare token 'refuses'. It does not say whether the host list is invalid, all native location fields are suppressed while the namespaced projection succeeds, or the complete required projection fails.

noPrimaryWhenProduced says 'refuses native location emission', while placementRule still unconditionally directs every related entry with a locationUri into relatedLocations. For a produced result with no qualifying primary but at least one related URI, the two clauses do not say whether relatedLocations is written or suppressed.

The primary condition is also expressed in terms of expected.produced, a golden-side field, inside the runtime machine mapping. The contract does not state the equivalent projection-time predicate outside a golden.

These alternatives matter because whole-projection failure, namespaced-only success, and partial native emission have different parity and required-output consequences. The contract can choose among them without minting a new D9 code, but it must choose.
shouldFix.impact: A future DR-006-active produced fixture cannot derive one expected native-location outcome for zero/multiple-primary host lists. Preview has no produced fixture, so the defect is held below blocker grade.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Define a validation branch before placement. State the runtime predicate and, for zero and multiple qualifying primaries, explicitly choose whether the entire projection fails through the existing host-owned output path or both native arrays are omitted while opensip.artifactRefs remains authoritative. Make placementRule conditional on that branch and name what 'refuses' targets.
